description.narrative:
FORUM-ASIA´s vision (long-term, impact level) is to build democratic, just, equitable and sustainable societies in Asia and beyond, where human rights of all individuals, groups, and peoples are fully realised, in accordance with international human rights standards and norms.
To fulfill this goal, FA has made it its mission (medium-term, outcome level) to strengthen movements for human rights and sustainable development through advocacy, capacity development and solidarity actions with human rights defenders and civil society organisations.
FA´s two strategic goals, as formulated in the Strategic plan for 2023-2027 :
1. Empowering civil society and marginalised communities promoting and protecting human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia.
2. Resilient Asian civil society and marginalised communities continuing their work for human rights, civic space and democracy in a safe and sustainable manner
There are six underlying objectives, including specific objectives related to Gender, Climate Crises and BHR:
1.1 Improved legal, policy, and regulatory environment for human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia
1.2 Increased accountability of state and non-state actors on human rights violations and abuses at national, regional and international levels
2.1 Increased protection and support for Asian Civil society and marginalised communities including those operating in conflict and climate crises situations to continue their work on human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia.
2.2 Improved operational resilience and holistic security of Asian civil society and marginalised communities including those operating in conflict and climate crisis situations to mitigate and respond to threats and attacks and sustain operations in online and offline spaces.
Climate Crises & Business and Human Rights: Strengthened promotion and protection of the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment of vulnerable and marginalised communities in the context of development projects and business operations.
Gender: Enhanced recognition and inclusion of the rights and issues of vulnerable groups of different gender identities and sexual orientation especially women and LGBTIQ groups in FA operations.
All the Specific Objectives have underlying Outcomes connected to them, as pre-conditions to the Specific Objectives.

Founded in 1991, The Asian Forum for Human Rights and Development (FORUM-ASIA) is a regional member based civil society organisation with 85 member organisations across 23 countries. FORUM-ASIA has consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) and a consultative relationship with the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR). The organisation is a longstanding partner to Sweden.
FORUM-ASIAs two strategic goals, as formulated in its Strategic Plan for 2023-2027: 1.Empowering civil society and marginalised communities promoting and protecting human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia. 2. Resilient Asian civil society and marginalised communities continuing their work for human rights, civic space and democracy in a safe and sustainable manner. There are also six underlying objectives, including specific objectives related to Gender, Climate Crisis and Business and Human Rights (B+HR).
There are opportunities for FORUM-ASIA to have a proactive, positive impact on peace and conflict dynamics, not least via its support to human security via the Human Rights Defenders Programme.

The Asian Forum for Human Rights and Development (FORUM-ASIA) grundades 1991. FORUM-ASIA är en regional, medlemsbaserad civilsamhällesorganisation med 85 medlemsorganisationer i 23 länder. Organisationen har en rådgivande status hos FN:s ekonomiska och sociala råd (ECOSOC) samt innehar en rådgivande relation till ASEAN:s mellanstatliga kommission för mänskliga rättigheter (AICHR). Organisationen är en flerårig samarbetspartner till Sverige.
FA:s två strategiska mål, så som formulerats i den strategiska planen för 2023-2027:
1. Stärka egenmakten hos de civilsamhällesaktörer och marginaliserade grupper som främjar och skyddar mänskliga rättigheter och det civila samhällets demokratiska utrymme. 2. Ett motståndskraftigt civilt samhälle i Asien, där civilsamhälle och marginaliserade grupper kan utföra sitt arbete för att stärka mänskliga rättigheter och det civila samhällets demokratiska utrymme på ett säkert och hållbart sätt.
FORUM-ASIA:s strategi innefattar sex underliggande mål, inklusive specifika mål relaterade till jämställdhet, miljö-och klimat samt företagande och mänskliga rättigheter (B+HR). Insatsens bedöms även vara relevant utifrån ett konfliktperspektiv, inte minst genom arbetet kopplat till mänsklig säkerhet, via deras Human Right Defenders Programme.

Examples of key results during the period:
1.1 Improved legal, policy and regulatory environment for human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia
- During the year, FA co-ordinated several joint civilsociety interventions directed at ASEAN, responding to the continued deterioration of civic space in the region. This included the publication of regional policy briefs on civicspace restrictions, coordinated statements endorsed by more than 100 member organisations, and direct engagement with the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR). As a result of this coordinated pressure, civicspace concerns in Myanmar, Cambodia and the Philippines were explicitly raised in ASEAN consultations and referenced in AICHR dialogue sessionsan outcome ForumAsia highlighted in its 2024 reporting as a key opening for continued policy influence.
1.2. Increased accountability of state and non-state actors on human rights violations and abuses at national, regional and international levels
- FAs report "Defending in Numbers 20232024" documented 1,577 cases of harassment against HRDs in 23 Asian countries, including judicial harassment, surveillance, and physical attacks. This evidence base was used to name specific state agencies and, in some cases, corporate actors complicit in abuses, strengthening demands for accountability.
- The programme Business and human rights published "Holding the Line: Community Resistance and Corporate Accountability in Asia", which compiled case studies of labour rights abuses, land grabs, environmental harm and reprisals against communities and workers. These cases explicitly linked corporate actors and state regulators to concrete harms, providing material for advocacy with governments, NHRIs, investors and UN mechanisms.
Using its documentation, FA coordinated advocacy towards ASEAN and other regional forums, calling out restrictive laws, emergency measures and security policies used to silence HRDs and communities. In the business and human rights sphere, FAs 2024 report was used to push for stronger national action plans, due diligence standards and remedy mechanisms, thereby increasing pressure on both states and corporations. On the global leve, FA submitted submissions to UN Special Procedures and treaty bodies, and engaged around the Human Rights Council (HRC) on situations such as shrinking civic space, reprisals against HRDs, and corporate abuses. These efforts aimed to secure stronger resolutions, public statements and recommendations directed at specific governments and, where relevant, companies.
2.1. Increased protection and support for Asian civil society and marginalized communities including those operating in conflict and climate crisis situations to continue their work on human rights, civic space and democracy in Asia.
- FA provided direct protection support by issuing emergency grants for legal fees, safe housing and medical costs; arranging shortterm relocation for HRDs facing imminent arrest or violence; and delivering digitalsecurity interventions such as securecommunication setups and rapid response to hacking and surveillance attempts. Community groups affected by land grabs, mining projects and environmental destruction received handson assistance to collect evidence, prepare complaints to National Human Rights Institutions, and submit cases to UN Special Procedures and regional mechanisms.
Through its member organisations, FA coordinated crossborder support for HRDs escaping military offensives in Myanmar, reprisals against protest leaders in Sri Lanka, and enforceddisappearance risks in Bangladesh.
FAs capacitybuilding programmes delivered practical training on digital safety, documentation standards, and how to use UN mechanisms, enabling Indigenous, environmental and women HRDs to continue operating despite surveillance, threats and shrinking civic space. These interventions strengthened the resilience of frontline groups working in conflictaffected and climatevulnerable areas.
2.2. Improved operational resilience and holistic security of Asian civil society and marginalized communities including those operating in conflict and climate crisis situations to mitigate and respond to threats and attacks and sustain operations in online and offline space
- FA provided emergency operational support, including funds to replace confiscated equipment, secure office spaces, restore hacked communication channels and cover essential organisational costs after raids or shutdown orders. HRDs and community groups in Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and climateaffected parts of Southeast Asia used this support to maintain core activities during periods of heightened risk.
FA improved holistic security by conducting tailored risk assessments with local organisations and providing concrete followup measures such as securecommunication systems, digitalsecurity hardening, and protocols for safe documentation and storage of sensitive information. Groups targeted by spyware, doxxing and online harassment reported increased ability to continue online organising without interruption.
FAs regional network enabled continuity of operations for organisations forced to relocate due to conflict or political repression. Crossborder coordination helped partners reestablish safe working environments, maintain staff wellbeing, and continue advocacy from exile. FA also supported communitybased organisations affected by land grabs, extractive projects and climaterelated displacement to strengthen internal systems for evidence collection, case management and engagement with regional mechanisms.
Specific Objective a. Strengthened the promotion and protection of the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment of vulnerable and marginalised communities in the context of development projects and business operations.
- FA supported communities affected by extractive industries, agribusiness, infrastructure projects and climaterelated displacement. FAs business and human rights programme documented concrete cases of land grabs, pollution, forced evictions and reprisals linked to corporate actors and state regulators. This evidence enabled affected communities to file complaints to National Human Rights Institutions, submit cases to UN Special Procedures, and demand stronger environmental safeguards in development planning.
FA provided handson support to community groups defending forests, rivers and ancestral lands, including training on evidence collection, environmental impact monitoring and safe documentation of corporaterelated abuses. Several groups used this support to halt or delay harmful projects, negotiate with local authorities, or secure public hearings on environmental impacts.
FA amplified community alerts from climatevulnerable and conflictaffected areas, including Indigenous communities resisting mining and hydropower projects. Through regional advocacy, FA pushed ASEAN and national governments to strengthen environmental protection standards, ensure free, prior and informed consent (FPIC), and address reprisals against environmental human rights defenders.
Specific Objective b. Enhanced recognition and inclusion of the rights and issues of vulnerable groups of different gender identities and sexual orientation especially women and LGBTIQ groups in FORUM-ASIA operations.
- FA increased the visibility and influence of women and LGBTIQ defenders in 2024 by ensuring they were directly involved in regional consultations, thematic dialogues and evidencegathering processes. Their inputs shaped FAs positions on civic space, environmental rights and business and human rights, resulting in programme plans and advocacy messages that explicitly addressed genderspecific risks and SOGIESCrelated discrimination.
FA issued public statements highlighting cases of genderbased violence, criminalisation of LGBTIQ people and targeted attacks on women HRDs. These interventions elevated gender and SOGIESC issues within regional human rights debates and ensured that violations affecting these groups were reflected in FAs submissions to UN Special Procedures and regional mechanisms.
Internally, FA strengthened its genderresponsive operational practices by applying gendersensitive risk assessments, adapting emergency support to the needs of women and LGBTIQ HRDs (including safehousing arrangements, traumainformed support and secure participation protocols), and ensuring that all trainings and regional events included safeguards for participants facing genderspecific threats.
